assetRisk.scenario: Off-specification finished fuel release or batch contamination requiring pipeline downgrade, pump-out, or remediation
assetRisk.source: ~10-11 refineries processing ~80 MMTPA (~1.6 Mbbl/d) delivering finished fuels into ~20,000 km of pipelines and ~120 terminals. Frequency (0.30) reflects ~1 significant off-specification batch release or multi-product pipeline contamination event per refinery every 3.3 years (~3.3 events/yr across the estate). Consequence (₹18 Cr / ~US$2.15M) covers: (1) product value downgrade margin loss (downgrading 40,000-80,000 bbl of contaminated prime gasoline/ULSD/ATF to slop oil or low-value fuel oil cutter stock at a ₹800-₹1,500/bbl price spread = ₹4-8 Cr); (2) off-spec slop re-refining, pump-out, and rail/truck logistics to return product to crude/hydrotreater feedstocks (₹4-6 Cr); (3) pipeline common-carrier tariff penalties, interface flushing, and transmix processing charges (₹2-4 Cr); and (4) statutory fuel specification non-compliance fines and customer/vehicle remediation claims under national standards (BIS IS 1460/2796, EPA 40 CFR Part 1090, OISD-RP-108) (₹2-4 Cr). Alpha (0.35) reflects the causal share attributable to analytical decision and data defects (undetected GC/XRF instrument drift, test results accepted within unflagged ASTM D6299/ISO 4259 guard-bands, missed thermodynamic property discordance between flash point and distillation, and delayed OOS investigations); beta (0.40) reflects the 7-agent squad's efficacy in autonomous ASTM D6299 SQC chart surveillance, thermodynamic screening, and structured ISO/IEC 17025 root-cause verification.

rationale: P50 Quality Control Chemist governs physical and chemical testing, instrument calibration hierarchies, statistical quality control (SQC), and Certificate of Analysis (CoA) certification across refinery intermediate streams and finished transportation fuels. Sizing at 260 seats represents ~0.84% of enterprise staff (~31,000), defensibly distributed across: ~205 laboratory chemists and officers across 11 refineries (averaging 18-19 per refinery, structured as 12-14 shift chemists providing continuous 24/7/365 coverage across 4 shift panels plus 5-6 day specialists in gas chromatography/SimDist, crude assay, CFR octane engines, and ISO/IEC 17025 QA); ~22 chemists supporting integrated petrochemical complexes (naphtha crackers, aromatics, polymers); ~20 quality control officers across ~25-30 major pipeline origin/dispatch terminals; and ~13 specialists in corporate quality assurance and aviation fuel quality inspection. Asset Capital is strictly null in accordance with value_model.js rules: laboratory testing occurs within climate-controlled testing facilities and does not sit on the critical path of continuous operating refinery units (which run continuously into buffer rundown tanks); claiming volume-based quality giveaway would directly double-count P28 (Blended Product Quality), claiming yield giveaway would double-count P16, and claiming demurrage would double-count P15/P40. Asset Risk captures avoided off-specification finished fuel releases and pipeline contamination incidents across 11 refineries (frequency 0.30/yr, consequence ₹18 Cr, alpha 0.35, beta 0.40, yielding ₹8.32 Cr/yr in avoided expected losses with alpha*beta held to 0.14, well below the 0.18 ceiling). Resource Recovery is strictly null as downstream laboratory certification operates past the extraction boundary and cannot alter subsurface recoverable reserves, satisfying the portfolio rule prohibiting joint Integrity and Recovery claims.
caveats: 1. Asset capital is maintained as null to protect the model's 'load-bearing zero' discipline and prevent double-counting with P28 (blend giveaway) and P15/P40 (marine demurrage). If an operator insists on parameterizing asset capital for P50, it should be formulated in time form as avoided finished tank release stagnation and rundown throttling during false-positive OOS re-testing: {form: 'time', asset: 'Finished product certification and tank release', units: 11, unitLabel: 'refineries', hoursPerYear: 8760, share: 0.0010, ratePerHour: 2500000, basis: '0.10% of refinery calendar hours saved by avoiding tank release bottlenecks and precautionary unit throttling (~8.8 h/refinery/yr)', source: '11 refineries; ₹25 L/hr discounted refinery margin rate; yields ~₹2.41 Cr/yr'}. Setting assetCapital to null remains strongly recommended. 2. Failure consequence assumes large integrated refining complexes where off-spec finished fuel enters a high-pressure multi-product pipeline or coastal export vessel, creating widespread contamination across downstream terminal tankage. 3. Alpha and beta strictly reflect automated informational decision support, statistical drift alerting, and dossier synthesis; physical sample preparation, bench calibration standard preparation, and statutory CoA release signatures remain with human laboratory professionals.
